beats.intro: Derivatives, module nine. [[sub]]Calls, puts, the underlying and a bond are all tied together by one no-arbitrage relationship: put-call parity.
beats.portfolios: [[a]]Consider two portfolios. [[fid]]The first is a fiduciary call: a call option, plus a risk-free bond that pays the exercise price at maturity. The bond covers the exercise cost, and the call gives the upside. [[prot]]The second is a protective put: the underlying, plus a put option. The put sets a floor under the price. [[tab]]At maturity, if the price ends below the exercise price, the call expires worthless and the bond pays X. The put is exercised, and the underlying plus the put are worth X. If the price ends above, both portfolios are worth the underlying price. [[pt]]The payoffs are identical in every scenario, so the two portfolios must cost the same today.
beats.parity: [[a]]That is put-call parity. The underlying plus the put equals the call plus the present value of the exercise price. It holds for European options with the same exercise price and expiry, on an underlying with no income. [[ex]]Biomian shares are at two ninety-five rupees. A six-month call at an exercise price of two sixty-five trades at fifty-nine, and the rate is four percent. [[bond]]The bond is worth two fifty-nine eighty-five. [[res]]So the put should cost two ninety-five minus fifty-nine minus two fifty-nine eighty-five, which is twenty-three eighty-five. [[arb]]If the put actually trades at thirty, the left side is too expensive. Sell the shares and the put, buy the call and the bond. You collect six rupees fifteen today, and every outcome at maturity nets to zero.
beats.blocks: [[a]]Rearranging the equation gives a recipe for each building block. [[put]]A long put is a long call, plus a long bond, minus the underlying. [[call]]A long call is the underlying, plus a put, minus the bond. [[und]]The underlying is a call, minus a put, plus a bond. [[bond]]And a bond is the underlying, plus a put, minus a call. [[cc]]A covered call is the underlying minus a call. By the same equation, that is a bond minus a put: a long bond, plus a sold put. [[ex]]Biomian again, at two ninety-five. A call at an exercise price of three twenty-five is replicated with a put priced at fifty-six. The bond is worth three eighteen sixty-nine, so the call must cost thirty-two thirty-one.
beats.forward: [[a]]The underlying can itself be replicated, with a long forward and a bond that pays the forward price. Substituting gives put-call forward parity. [[eq]]The present value of the forward price, plus the put, equals the call, plus the present value of the exercise price. [[diff]]Rearranged, a long put and a short call equals a long bond and a short forward, with a value equal to the exercise price minus the forward price, discounted. [[ex]]For Biomian, the forward price is three hundred rupees and eighty-four paise. The put works out to twenty-three eighty-six, the same as before, apart from rounding.
beats.firm: [[a]]Put-call parity even explains a company's capital structure. Suppose a firm owes debt with a face value D, due at time T. [[solv]]If the firm's value then exceeds D, debtholders are repaid in full and shareholders keep the rest. [[insol]]If it falls short, debtholders take everything the firm has, and shareholders get nothing. [[eq]]So shareholders hold a call option on the firm's assets, with the debt as the exercise price. [[debt]]Debtholders hold a risk-free bond, and have sold a put option to the shareholders. [[v]]Applying parity, the firm's value equals the call, plus the present value of debt, minus the put. Shareholders have unlimited upside and limited downside. Debtholders' upside is capped at repayment.
beats.wrap: [[w1]]A fiduciary call and a protective put have identical payoffs, so they cost the same. [[w2]]Put-call parity: underlying plus put equals call plus the present value of the exercise price. [[w3]]Any mispricing is a riskless arbitrage, and any one position can be built from the others. [[w4]]Equity is a call on the firm, and risky debt is a bond minus a put.
beats.finish: Module nine complete. Next: the one-period binomial model.
